key_insight: Ultrasonic-assisted friction stir welding adds high-frequency vibration to FSW, improving metal flow, reducing loads, and refining weld microstructure in aluminum alloys.
engineering_relevance: The review highlights UAFSW as a practical route to join high-strength and dissimilar aluminum alloys with fewer defects and better mechanical performance.
method: Integrate ultrasonic vibration with the FSW thermal-mechanical field.
Exploit acoustic volume and surface effects to enhance plasticized metal rheology and grain refinement.
Compare process parameters and reported outcomes across similar and dissimilar aluminum alloy joints.
evidence_signal: The paper synthesizes recent experimental studies and representative process data showing improved microstructure and mechanical properties in UAFSW joints.
watch_item: Performance gains depend strongly on ultrasonic setup and welding parameters, so benefits may not transfer uniformly across alloys or joint types.
paper_title: Recent Progress in Process and Mechanical Properties of Ultrasonic-Assisted Friction Stir Welding of Aluminum Alloys: A Review
